InsertQuery.role: An ordinary positional INSERT from an independent one-source SELECT.
InsertQuery.structure: An absolute writable target with signed INT and native VARCHAR positions, and an owned checked SELECT of the same width. Each VARCHAR position admits a text literal, native VARCHAR slot, explicit native text collation or SQL NULL. Each signed position retains its signed operands and SQL NULL.
InsertQuery.conditions: The independent SELECT has no joins, ORDER BY or LIMIT. Require exact position correspondence and a compatible native expression type at every destination before publication. The source declares and checks each read scope independently of the target.
InsertQuery.rightOfUse: Direct constructors and the ordinary analyzed INSERT SELECT entry route use the same positional boundary. Incompatible implicit conversions remain separate obligations.
InsertQuery.meaning: Evaluate the source predicate and projection before native assignment into the ordered destination list. DISTINCT tests the projected values using their source type and stock PAD SPACE equivalence, before character truncation or NULL substitution. A tied DISTINCT class permits an actual whole source-row representative and preserves its byte values.
InsertQuery.sql: Render the exact qualified target and ordered field list, followed by the independently scoped checked SELECT with its projections, DISTINCT and predicate. Preserve the native query INSERT form even for zero or one resulting row.

externalInterpretation: Use fixed, disjoint InnoDB source and target fixtures. The resolved declarations include the same collations, capacity, nullability and ordered fields as the native fixture. Target defaults and the AFTER INSERT trigger reside in the fixture.
observations: Exact affected row count and typed target cell contents after positional assignment
Unchanged populated and empty source tables and the independent control table
Native empty-mode warning severity, code, destination and multiplicity, including NULL assigned to a required field and multibyte truncation
Ordered trigger events accounting for an admitted traversal of unordered source rows, complete transactional restoration and original rows including duplicates
effects: Every SELECT-selected SQL NULL assigned to a required VARCHAR becomes the implicit empty value with native warning 1048, including a one-row SELECT. A source string beyond the character capacity is truncated at a character boundary. Important discarded characters produce Warning 1265. In the registered fixture a direct VARCHAR field copy, or a DISTINCT-materialized explicitly collated field, reports Warning 1265 even for discarded ASCII padding. Plain and explicitly collated constants and nonmaterialized explicitly collated fields report Note 1265 when only ASCII padding is discarded. Diagnostic source ordinals appear in the raw transcript and must be positive. Row visitation and optimizer-dependent diagnostic ordinals from an unordered SELECT have no fixed ordering contract.
change: Preserve exact error levels, codes, destinations and counts. The native calibration separates direct field copies, ordinary text expressions and materialized DISTINCT text fields. Keep every original fixture, case, budget and fault obligation.

counterexample.observed: All nine releases returned Note 1265 after discarding the final ASCII space from a collated constant. The original verifier predicted a Warning. Independent native probes over ordinary and DISTINCT queries reproduce the field-copy and expression cases and retain the original failed ledgers.

comparison: For ALL, consume exactly one matching raw projected record per observed insertion. For DISTINCT, consume exactly one representative from each independent whole-row equivalence class. Compare the stored rows as a bag and match the trigger event sequence to that finite admission relation. Preserve the exact event position and multiplicity. Compare warning multiplicity for an admitted row selection, with the release-specific repeated required-NULL diagnostic rule. Compare the full snapshot after rollback to the independently constructed initial state.

finite.completeness: Recover layout, source, filter or NULL input and DISTINCT from the actual constructed values and compare their identities with a separate Cartesian enumeration.

exploration.requiredForms: Observe one through four target fields, both source cardinalities, raw and native explicit text roles, alternate source positions, signed positions, optional filters, duplicate aliases, zero-capacity, required and nullable destinations, Unicode and terminal padding.
